title: feat(console): a settings info_banner speaks the session locale, draws a warning in amber and renders its body as Markdown (objectui#12671)
body:
Fixes #12671
Clause-②: no (the console starts reading a slot the platform already declares, `settings.NAMESPACE.banners.BANNER_ID.{title,text}`, objectstack-ai/objectstack#23886; it publishes no new export, prop or accepted key)

## What changes

A settings page's `info_banner` row:

1. **Speaks the session locale.** `useSettingsLabel` gains `bannerTitle(bannerId, fallback)` and `bannerText(bannerId, fallback)`. They read `settings.NAMESPACE.banners.BANNER_ID.title` and `.text` through the hook's existing `resolve()`, with the same namespace discovery, the same exists-first probe and the same manifest-literal fallback as `groupTitle`, and the docblock lists both paths. The `info_banner` arm of `SettingsField` asks them when `spec.id` is set, exactly as the `group` arm asks `groupTitle`. This mirrors the platform readers `resolveSettingsBannerTitle` / `resolveSettingsBannerText` in objectstack's `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`. No other spelling is read: a singular `banner` branch, a `notices` branch, a `bannerText` leaf and a `label` leaf are each pinned as not consulted.
2. **Draws a warning in amber** (objectui#12610 target 2). `bannerSeverity: 'warning'` lays the shell's existing amber callout spelling over the `default` Alert, with the warning triangle in amber as its icon. `error` stays `destructive`; `info`, `success` and an unset severity keep `default`. No new Alert variant, and `packages/components/src/ui/` is untouched. The arm's `variant as any` cast is gone: the ternary already has the variant's type.
3. **Renders its body as Markdown**, as the spec declares (`bannerText: z.string().optional().describe('Markdown body (info_banner)')` in objectstack's `settings-manifest.zod.ts`). It goes through the docs portal's renderer, `MarkdownRenderer` from `@object-ui/plugin-markdown` (the one `DocPage` draws a package doc with), and its unconditional `rehype-sanitize` pass, used as it is. No new dependency: the console already depends on the plugin.

The bundle is read untyped through `resolve()`, as the `groups` helper reads it, so nothing waits on `@objectstack/spec` next.3.

## The renderer, and why it loads lazily

`SettingsField` is in the console's eager closure: `AppContent` imports `WorkspaceTimezonePrompt`, which imports it. A static import of the plugin would put the plugin's chunk, highlighter included, on every page load. So the arm loads `MarkdownRenderer` through `React.lazy` over `import('@object-ui/plugin-markdown')`, the specifier `DocPage` and the registry's lazy `markdown` loader already use, and the Suspense fallback is the body's own plain text.

Measured with a production console build on this branch (`66556f0`) against the same build with the two source files at the base `e6175b5`. Every dependency `dist/` is identical between the two, since this diff touches no package. The readings come from `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`:

| | base `e6175b5` | this branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| eager chunks / all chunks | 70 / 2253 | 70 / 2253 |
| eager closure, gzipped bytes | 3,193,363 | 3,193,677 (+314) |
| `SettingsField` chunk (eager) | 2,870 | 3,163 (+293) |
| `useSettingsLabel` chunk (eager) | 1,468 | 1,488 (+20) |
| `index` chunk | 67,615 | 67,616 (+1) |

The `plugin-markdown` chunk is not in the eager list on either build, and the eager `SettingsField` chunk reaches it only through a dynamic `import()`. `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` on this branch's build: `✅ Console eager closure is 3118.8 KB gzipped across 70 of 2253 chunks (budget: 3744.1 KB, headroom: 625.3 KB)`, exit 0.

Two other renderers were considered and not used:

- **The registry's `markdown` type through `SchemaRenderer`**, which `DocPreview` uses. Rejected because `SchemaRenderer` evaluates a node's `content` string as a `${…}` template, so the banner text would be interpreted as an expression. Its lazy placeholder is also an untranslated `Loading markdown…` line.
- **`MarkdownCellRenderer` from `@object-ui/fields`**, which is already eager and would cost zero bytes. Rejected because it is a cell renderer whose props require a `field: FieldMetadata` it never reads, so the banner would have to forge one.

## Premise checks on `origin/main` `e6175b5`

- **H1 holds.** The `info_banner` arm drew `literalLabel` and `spec.bannerText` as literals and mapped only `error` to `destructive`. The `group` arm asked `labels.groupTitle(spec.id, literalLabel)`.
- **H2: two renderers exist.** `DocPage`'s `MarkdownRenderer` is the one for a trusted body (package-authored text, as a manifest's banner is), so it is the one used. The heavy-module case is avoided by loading it lazily, measured above.
- **H3: no warning spelling in the design system.** The `Alert` primitive declares only `default` and `destructive`. The console declares a `--warning` token, but it is a 50%-lightness amber, about 2.1:1 on white, too pale for body text, and only one dot on the login page uses it. The amber callouts across the shell spell it with the amber palette, so the arm uses the `border-amber-300/60 bg-amber-50 text-amber-800` spelling with its dark pair (`dark:border-amber-700/50 dark:bg-amber-950/30 dark:text-amber-200`), as `PermissionMatrixEditor`'s and `SuggestedBindingsPanel`'s notices do. The icon takes `text-amber-600` / `dark:text-amber-400`, the shell's warning-glyph amber.
- **H4: `resolve()` holds.** It discovers every top-level namespace in the current language's bundle that has a `settings` member, asks `i18n.exists()` before `t()` (objectui#11801), and returns the fallback on a miss. `transformSpecTranslations` carries `settings` through untouched, so `banners` arrives under `app` as served. The two helpers call that same `resolve()` with `banners.BANNER_ID.title` / `.text`.

## Tests

New: `apps/console/src/pages/settings/__tests__/SettingsField.infoBanner-12671.test.tsx` (16 tests) and `apps/console/src/pages/settings/__tests__/useSettingsLabel.banners-12671.test.tsx` (4 tests). They pin:

- a bundle with `settings.NAMESPACE.banners.ID.{title,text}` renders the translated pair, and a miss renders the manifest literals;
- each half translates on its own;
- none of the four other spellings is consulted;
- no helper is asked without an `id`;
- `warning` draws amber, with tailwind-merge dropping the default colours; `error` stays destructive; `info`, `success` and unset stay default;
- a Markdown body renders a code element, a strong element and a link, and a translated body goes through the same renderer;
- at the hook, the two paths, the namespace scoping, the fallbacks, and the objectui#11801 no-warning property, with a live-channel control.

Both lazy boundaries are imported at module scope in the arm suite, so no `findBy` races the module loader.

### Ablations (each mutation landed and was restored through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`; every run then read `git diff HEAD` empty)

| # | mutation | failed / passed, and which pins went red |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | the arm's title back to `literalLabel` | 2 / 14: the translated pair, the title-only half |
| A2 | the arm's body back to `spec.bannerText` | 1 / 15: the translated pair |
| A3 | the title helper reads `banner.` (singular) | 5 / 15 across both suites, including the singular-branch negative pin |
| A4 | the text helper reads `.body` | 2 / 18: hook paths, translated pair |
| A5 | the title helper drops its fallback | 3 / 17: the miss-renders-literals pins |
| A6 | the title helper also reads `banner.` as an alias | 1 / 15: the singular-branch negative pin |
| A7 | the arm asks the helper without an `id` | 1 / 15: the no-id pin |
| A8 | the amber classes dropped | 1 / 15: warning draws amber |
| A9 | amber widened to every non-error severity | 3 / 13: info, success, unset |
| A10 | `error` no longer `destructive` | 1 / 15 |
| A11 | the body as a plain text child | 10 / 6: the Markdown pin and every body read through the renderer |
| A12 | the text helper also calls a plain `t()` | 1 / 3: the no-warning pin (its control leg proves the channel is live) |

### Runs, all on `66556f0`

- New suites: `pnpm exec vitest run` over the two files gives `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 20 passed (20)`.
- The console package, plus the three suites outside it that read these modules: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 apps/console/ packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/select-placeholder-literal-11252.test.ts packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/bootRedirectCoverage.test.tsx scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-dead-keys.test.ts` gives `Test Files 214 passed (214)`, `Tests 2389 passed (2389)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check`, after the console's dependency closure build (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/console^...'`, 34 tasks successful): exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` includes both new test files and the plugin's `MarkdownImpl.tsx`.
- `eslint` on the four changed source and test files: 0 errors. The 2 warnings are pre-existing `any`s outside the arm; the file had 3 before this diff.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, 1 changeset for 1 released package. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `0 new citation(s)`, exit 0. `pnpm check:i18n-keys`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-test-path-roots.mjs`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-vi-mock-override-shape.mjs`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the five paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- Everything else (`pnpm lint`, `pnpm check`, the test shards, Bundle Analysis) runs in CI.

### Browser reading

Chromium, on a throwaway preview page served by the console's Vite dev server. The page was not committed.

- Light: the warning Alert computes `bg` amber-50, text amber-800, a 60% amber-300 border and an amber-600 icon.
- Dark: amber-950 at 30%, text amber-200, icon amber-400.
- The env-var example in the Feature Flags notice draws as a code element. The body paragraph is 14 px with 0 margin.
- `error` keeps the destructive title and border; `info` keeps the default callout.

## Acceptance notes

- **Body colour.** The Markdown body takes the renderer's prose body colour (the foreground) in every severity. The title, border and icon carry the severity. On `error` the body used to inherit the destructive red, and it now reads in the foreground colour. Measured in the browser reading above; no live producer declares `error` today.
- **13 px not applied.** objectui#12610 target 2 asked for "amber, 13 px, icon". The severity changes colour and icon only, and every banner keeps the Alert's sizes (14 px body).
- **`success` stays neutral.** This card scopes `warning` and `error`, so `success` keeps the neutral callout.
- **First-load skeleton.** `MarkdownRenderer` has its own Suspense fallback, a 200 px skeleton. In the production build the plugin's index and its `MarkdownImpl` share the one `plugin-markdown` chunk, so that window is one resolved import. NOT MEASURED in a production browser session; observed only on the dev server, where the body showed as plain text and then as Markdown.
- **The `App.tsx` comment.** It says `DocPage` is "the only console-owned module that reaches `@object-ui/plugin-markdown`". Read as static reach it still holds, and the plugin stays behind a lazy boundary (measured above). `register-plugins.ts` already reached the plugin dynamically before this diff. Not edited: outside this card's file surface.
